youtube_description:
Why do many t-shirts commonly use a different stitch at the hem than at the side seams? Learn what a twin-needle 406 coverseam and a three-thread 504 overedge usually do, why two-thread 503 serging is not suitable for a loaded joining seam, and why two visible rows alone don't tell you the stitch type or certify quality. Always confirm the stitch type with your supplier. Not every T-shirt is built the same way; tubular garments may have no side seams.
